relevance_note: Case report of a boy with Blau syndrome carrying a de novo heterozygous NOD2 variant ('we present an 11-month-old boy with Blau syndrome'), plus a literature table of three earlier patients with NOD2 genotypes.
method_note: Read the paper fully and built the JSON with a short Python script; every value was typed from my reading and every span was checked by script to occur verbatim. The case-report patient is labelled 'patient' (rule 5; the Table 1 header 'This patient' is a role word). Table 1 shows patients as columns: column 1 'Borzutzky et.al. [8] 2010', column 2 'Lo et.al. [7] 2018', column 3 'Whyte et. al. [3] 2018', column 4 'This patient'. Each earlier report is treated as one patient (the table gives one value per report); these three are labelled 'Table 1 column 1/2/3' with the header copied into source_reference_in_review. Table 1 has four rows all labelled 'Other symptoms (onset)'; spans quote from that label through the patient's cell. Table notes define H high, L low, N normal; Lo's 1,25(OH)2 vitamin D '64 (N)' is recorded as excluded 'elevated 1,25(OH)2 vitamin D' (D-27). N/A cells are not reported. Inheritance 'de novo' rests on 'Trio genome sequencing identified a de novo heterozygous pathogenic variant' (trio = both parents sequenced; the paper does not separately state the parents' results). The variant is printed as 'c.920G>A (p.Arg307Gln)' in Results and Table 1 and as 'c.920G> A [p.Arg307Gln]' in the Discussion. Time-qualified absences for the patient (no musculoskeletal involvement at the time of hypercalcemia; none of arthritis, dermatitis, uveitis at disease onset) are recorded as excluded rows with the time in severity_or_detail; they are not contradictions because the features developed later, so the checklist marks arthritis, dermatitis and uveitis observed. Age at onset of the patient taken as the hypercalcemic presentation at 11 months, which the paper calls the initial manifestation; the paper also reports recurrent infections from 7 months and failure to thrive from 10 months. Age at last evaluation is not stated in the text (Supplementary Table 1, a timeline of the acute hypercalcemia management, ends at '2 Yr 1 mo'; its PDF-converted columns are misaligned, so it was used only for the patient's rash wording, polyarthritis and band keratopathy). Country/ethnicity not stated for the patient (only the institution in Bangkok and Thai genome databases), so left not reported. 'Impaired renal function' (Discussion) recorded as a feature but the checklist item 'granulomatous nephritis or renal failure' left not reported. Whyte's 'Joint swollen' was taken as arthritis or joint synovitis observed; Borzutzky's 'Migratory rashes' as skin rash observed. No contradictions found otherwise.
